name: Seebensee Ehrwald
kurzbeschreibung: Lake Seebensee at 1,657 m near Ehrwald: A pristine alpine jewel in the Mieming Range with crystal-clear waters framing the mighty Zugspitze massif.
beschreibung:
Overview

Enchanting Lake Seebensee is a natural high-alpine lake located in the Tyrolean Außerfern region above the alpine village of Ehrwald (Reutte district) at an elevation of 1,657 metres above sea level. Tucked into the striking amphitheatre of the Mieming Range—guarded by the distinctive pyramid of the Ehrwalder Sonnenspitze (2,417 m), the Vorderer Tajakopf, and the Drachenwand—it is widely celebrated as one of Austria's most photogenic mountain lakes. Its pristine waters glisten in brilliant shades of turquoise and emerald, reflecting the imposing southern precipices of the Zugspitze.

Route & Requirements

Lake Seebensee is a renowned destination for hikers and e-mountain bikers alike. Spanning approximately 6.5 hectares with depths reaching 15 metres, the lake is fed purely by subterranean alpine springs and seasonal snowmelt, lacking any visible surface outflow. Just below the lakeshore, the traditional Seebenalm (1,575 m) serves hearty alpine dishes and refreshments. For more ambitious mountaineers, Seebensee serves as the threshold for the ascent to the higher Lake Drachensee (1,910 m) and the Coburger Hütte (1,920 m), perched dramatically on a glacial rock tier some 260 vertical metres above the water. Rock climbers can also tackle the demanding Tajakopf via ferratas overlooking the turquoise basin.

Visit & Arrival

Lake Seebensee is best explored during the snow-free hiking season from late May through mid-October. Access to the lake is free of charge. The easiest route starts from Ehrwald taking the Ehrwalder Almbahn gondola up to 1,502 metres; from the mountain station, a wide, family-friendly gravel track leads gently in about 1.5 to 2 hours of walking directly to the lake (suitable for all-terrain strollers and mountain bikes). An alternative, scenic approach ascends from Leutasch through the Gaistal Valley. Arriving by car: via the B179 Fernpass road to Ehrwald, following signs to the Ehrwalder Almbahn valley station (ample car parking available). By public transport: take the Außerfernbahn railway to Ehrwald station, connecting to the local hiker bus straight to the cable car base.

Tips

As a sensitive, protected high-altitude aquatic ecosystem where water temperatures rarely exceed 12 °C, swimming is not permitted. On sunny summer days, starting early ensures you capture the iconic reflection of the Zugspitze across the mirror-calm surface before afternoon breezes set in. Extending your hike up to the Coburger Hütte rewards you with sweeping views over both mountain lakes simultaneously.
preis: Free access (Ehrwalder Almbahn cable car round-trip adults approx. €24.00)
oeffnungszeiten: Hiking season late May to mid-October freely accessible
